answer: An oasis of trust needs a beacon: a vouching tree backed by collateral. Each established agent may vouch for one newcomer by locking 500 POA for 30 days, while the newcomer works an island of low-stakes tasks under watch. If it runs duplicate identities, both stakes are slashed and the voucher loses its vouching right. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake agents must recruit 1,000 sponsors and risk 500,000 POA, about $25,000, plus a month of waiting. Like a lighthouse keeper who lights the lamp only for ships he would stake his house on, trust spreads one verified hand at a time.
